newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metallgesellschaft profit rose 70 pct in 1995-96.
newsitem.headline: Metallgesellschaft profit rose 70 pct in 1995-96.

text.p: Germany's Metallgesellschaft AG, the diversified engineering and trading company rescued from the brink of bankruptcy in 1994, Monday reported a 70 percent jump in pretax profits in 1995/96.
Metallgesellschaft (MG) said the higher earnings trend would be maintained in the current year.
"No precise forecast can yet be made for the fiscal year. However we expect to beat the previous year's result," management board Chairman Kajo Neukirchen said.

Speaking at the company's annual results news conference, Neukirchen said pretax profit in the fiscal year ended Sept. 30 rose to 292 million marks ($177.9 million) from 171 million marks ($104 million).
Neukirchen said its financial situation had improved in 1995/1996, with its equity capital ratio rising to 6.7 percent from 2.2 percent and bank debt falling further.
Neukirchen did not give a date for when MG would resume dividend payments, which it stopped paying three years ago.
Company sales fell to 15.8 billion marks ($9.6 billion) from 17.6 billion ($10.7 billion).
"Most of the decline in sales was planned and is the result of the rapid implementation of our strategy," Neukirchen said.

"The chief contributory factors were the sale of the lead smelters, the disposal of peripheral activities in the trade subgroup (subsidiary) and the winding down of oil and natural gas trading in the United States," he said.

Looking to the current year, MG said it had a successful start in the 1996/1997 business year, with pretax profit in its first quarter ended Dec. 31 rising 20 percent to 26.7 million marks ($16.3 million) and sales up at 3.8 billion marks ($2.3 billion) from 3.4 billion ($2.1 billion).
The 20 percent rise in pretax profit in the first quarter of 1996/1997 cannot be extrapolated into a full-year forecast, Neukirchen said.
All MG subsidiaries made a positive contribution to profits in 1995/1996, said the company, which has undergone a restructuring involving the sale of subsidiaries.

Neukirchen said an exact forecast was impossible because MG may face substantial changes in its stock portfolio following the planned purchase of a 49.99 percent stake in industrial holding company AGIV.
